newsitem.title: USA: Flower company executive to plead guilty to fraud.
newsitem.headline: Flower company executive to plead guilty to fraud.

text.p: George Heublein, whose Oregon flower bulb company drew $52 million from investors before it collapsed and he fled, has agreed to plead guilty to federal fraud and tax charges, his lawyer said Friday.
Heublein, 62, will plead guilty Monday before U.S. District Judge Helen Frye on two of the 21 charges for which he was indicted, said the attorney, Norman Sepenuk.
He is being held in the federal detention center in Sheridan, Ore.

He had been indicted in 1991 for conspiracy, tax violations, securities fraud, money laundering and similar offenses. He remained fugitive from the time the Oregon company collapsed in 1987 until last year, when he was arrested in Hollywood, Fla., where he worked as a grocery bagger.
He was found to hold U.S. and Salvadoran passports with stamps indicating wide travel. Records showed he had used eight aliases and had bank accounts in Switzerland, Egypt and Panama.

Two of his former executives have been convicted of fraud, and Heublein faces a judgment of $250 million from a class-action lawsuit by investors. Stockbrokers and accountants who aided his securities sales have been fined a total of $89 million.
